parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 1: Introduction to Aqidah & Fiqh
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A simple, elegant title slide. Background showing a traditional manuscript design or geometric patterns. Emphasize the keywords: *Aqidah* (Creed) and *Fiqh* (Jurisprudence).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Welcome to our Islamic Studies Journey!**
  * **Aqidah (عَقِيدَة):** The firm belief in our hearts about Allah, the Prophets, and the unseen.
  * **Fiqh (فِقْه):** The practical rules of how we worship and live our lives.
  * Why do we learn specific schools of thought (*Madhhabs*)?
    * To build deep legal and theological literacy.
    * To appreciate the rich diversity of Islamic scholarship.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Start the class by explaining that Islam is not flat or uniform in every detail of practice and sub-theology. Scholars have preserved different, valid paths.
  * Introduce the *Ash'ari* (أَشْعَرِي) school of theology and the *Maliki* (مَالِكِي) school of law. Explain that these are followed by millions of Muslims, particularly in North and West Africa, parts of the Middle East, and historically in Muslim Spain (Al-Andalus).
  * Emphasize to the students that seeing differences in how people pray (like where they place their hands) is a sign of mercy and scholarly depth, not division.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 2: Who is Allah? The Core Principle of Tawhid
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 2: Who is Allah? The Core Principle of Tawhid
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A starry night sky or a beautiful nature background. Central word: *Tawhid* (تَوْحِيد) in clean, prominent text.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Tawhid (تَوْحِيد):** Uncompromising belief in the Oneness of Allah.
  * Allah is *Al-Wahid* (الْوَاحِد) and *Al-Ahad* (الأَحَد) – The One, The Unique.
  * He has no partners, no parents, no children, and no equals.
  * Knowing Allah is the very first obligation (*Wajib*) for a Muslim.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that *Tawhid* is the foundation of everything. In the Ash'ari school, the first obligation upon a person who reaches the age of mental maturity (*Bulugh*) is to know Allah through reason and revelation.
  * Discuss Surah al-Ikhlas (Chapter 112) as the ultimate summary of Tawhid. Highlight the word *Al-Samad* (الصَّمَد) – the Self-Sufficient Master upon whom all creation depends, while He depends on nothing.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 3: Knowing Allah through His Necessary Attributes (Sifat al-Wajibah)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 3: Knowing Allah through His Necessary Attributes (Sifat al-Wajibah)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A table or split column layout showing the Arabic terms on one side and English translations on the other.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Sifat al-Wajibah (الصِّفَات الْوَاجِبَة):** The attributes that logically must belong to Allah.
  * Ash'ari scholars identify **20 necessary attributes** divided into groups:
    1. *Nafsiyyah* (Personal): **Wujud** (Existence).
    2. *Salbiyyah* (Negative/Divesting): Attributes that deny what is impossible for Allah (e.g., having a beginning or end).
    3. *Ma'ani* (Existential/Qualitative): Power, Will, Knowledge, Life, Hearing, Sight, Speech.
    4. *Ma'nawiyyah* (Active/State): Being Powerful, Being Willful, etc.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that "negative attributes" (*Salbiyyah*) do not mean "bad." They mean attributes that negate or strip away any qualities of imperfection from Allah. For example, *Qidam* (Beginninglessness) negates that Allah was created.
  * Keep it simple for younger students: Allah is alive (*Hayy*), knows everything (*'Alim*), can do all things (*Qadir*), wills everything (*Murid*), hears everything (*Sami'*), sees everything (*Basir*), and speaks (*Mutakallim*). We will explore these one by one.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 4: Transcending Space and Time (Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 4: Transcending Space and Time (Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Graphic illustrating a timeline and a globe, with a barrier or indicator showing Allah is completely outside and beyond these concepts.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith (مُخَالَفَتُهُ لِلْحَوَادِثِ):** Absolute difference from created things.
  * Allah is not a physical body (*Jirm*). He does not occupy space.
  * Allah created space and time; therefore, He is not contained by them.
  * *"There is nothing like unto Him, and He is the Hearing, the Seeing."* (Surah ash-Shura, 42:11)
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * This is a cornerstone of Ash'ari theology: *Tanzih* (تَنْزِيه), which means declaring Allah free of any resemblance to His creation.
  * Explain that everything we can imagine in our minds is a creation. Since Allah is the Creator, He cannot look like, sound like, or be like anything we can imagine. 
  * If a student asks, "Where is Allah?", the teacher should explain: Allah exists without a place (*Makan*). He created "above" and "below," so He is not physically inside or limited by directions.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 5: The Names of Allah (Al-Asma' al-Husna)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 5: The Names of Allah (Al-Asma' al-Husna)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A collage of beautiful calligraphy of some of the 99 Names, such as *Al-Khaliq* (The Creator), *Al-Rahman* (The Merciful), and *Al-Hakim* (The Wise).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Al-Asma' al-Husna (الأَسْمَاء الْحُسْنَى):** The Most Beautiful Names of Allah.
  * The Prophet ﷺ said: *"Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. Whoever guards/memorizes them will enter Paradise."* (Sahih al-Bukhari)
  * We use these Names to understand Allah's actions and how He cares for us.
  * Examples:
    * **Al-Ghaffar (الْغَفَّار):** The Repeatedly Forgiving.
    * **Al-Razzaq (الرَّزَّاق):** The Provider.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Emphasize that memorizing the Names is not just repeating them like a list; it means understanding their meanings and living by them.
  * Connect the Names to daily life: when we make a mistake, we call upon *Al-Ghaffar*; when we need help or food, we call upon *Al-Razzaq*; when we see the beautiful organization of the universe, we praise *Al-Hakim*.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 6: Ash'ari Reading of Sacred Texts: Tafwid and Ta'wil
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 6: Ash'ari Reading of Sacred Texts: Tafwid and Ta'wil
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A scale balance showing two valid paths: *Tafwid* (leaving the meaning to Allah) and *Ta'wil* (metaphorical interpretation).
* **Slide Content:**
  * How do we understand Quranic words like the "Hand" (*Yad*) or "Face" (*Wajh*) of Allah?
  * **Option A: Tafwid (تَفْوِيض) - The Way of the Salaf (Early Scholars)**
    * We say: We believe in the word as Allah revealed it, but we do not give it a physical meaning, and we say "Allah knows best what it means."
  * **Option B: Ta'wil (تَأْوِيل) - The Way of the Khalaf (Later Scholars)**
    * We interpret the word metaphorically using proper Arabic rules.
    * *Yad* (Hand) = Power (*Qudrah*) or Favor (*Ni'mah*).
    * *Istiwa'* (Establishing over the Throne) = Domination/Control (*Istila'*).
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * This slide is crucial for theological literacy. It teaches students that the Quran contains metaphorical language.
  * Explain that both *Tafwid* and *Ta'wil* are valid, orthodox Sunni paths. They both agree on one primary rule: **Allah does not have physical body parts.** 
  * Warn against *Tashbih* (تَشْبِيه) (anthropomorphism / comparing Allah to humans) and *Tajsim* (تَجْسِيم) (giving Allah a physical body). These are rejected in Sunni Aqidah.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 7: The Six Pillars of Iman (Overview)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 7: The Six Pillars of Iman (Overview)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An infographic showing six pillars supporting a beautiful structure labeled *Iman* (Faith).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Iman (إِيمَان):** Faith or belief.
  * The Hadith of Jibril: The Prophet ﷺ was asked about Iman and replied that it is to believe in:
    1. **Allah** (اللّٰه)
    2. His **Angels** (مَلَائِكَة)
    3. His **Books** (كُتُب)
    4. His **Messengers** (رُسُل)
    5. The **Last Day** (الْيَوْم الْآخِر)
    6. **Qadar** (قَدَر) - Divine Decree, both its good and its evil.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Remind the students of the difference between *Islam* (submission/physical actions like praying and fasting) and *Iman* (internal belief/conviction of the heart).
  * Use the Hadith of Jibril as the reference point. In it, Angel Jibril came in the form of a man in white clothing to teach the Sahabah (Companions) their religion.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 8: Iman in Allah and His Attributes of Power, Will, and Knowledge
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 8: Iman in Allah and His Attributes of Power, Will, and Knowledge
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Interlocking circles or gears showing *Qudrah* (Power), *Iradah* (Will), and *'Ilm* (Knowledge) working together.
* **Slide Content:**
  * Under Ash'ari Aqidah, three key attributes explain how Allah acts in the universe:
  * **Al-'Ilm (الْعِلْم) - Divine Knowledge:**
    * Allah knows everything eternally.
    * He knows what was, is, will be, and what *could* have been.
  * **Al-Iradah (الإِرَادَة) - Divine Will:**
    * Allah chooses to make things happen in a specific way, at a specific time, with specific qualities.
  * **Al-Qudrah (الْقُدْرَة) - Divine Power:**
    * Allah brings things from non-existence into existence.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Help students understand the relationship: Allah's *'Ilm* knows that a leaf will fall from a tree at 3:00 PM. His *Iradah* wills that this specific leaf falls at 3:00 PM rather than 4:00 PM. His *Qudrah* is the power that physically makes the leaf drop.
  * Emphasize that Allah's knowledge does not change; He does not "learn" new things. His knowledge is eternal.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 9: Angels: Creation, Nature, and Characteristics
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 9: Angels: Creation, Nature, and Characteristics
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Bright light rays against a deep background. Emphasize that angels are not human-like babies with wings, but majestic creations of light.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Angels (Malā'ikah - مَلَائِكَة):** Noble creations of Allah made from light (*Nur*).
  * They do not have physical genders (they are neither male nor female).
  * They do not eat, drink, sleep, or get tired.
  * They do not possess free will in the way humans do:
    * *"They do not disobey Allah in what He commands them, and they do what they are commanded."* (Surah at-Tahrim, 66:6)
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Clarify common cultural misconceptions: Angels in Islam are not "people who died and got wings." They are a completely different species created before humans.
  * Discuss their size and power. For example, Jibril is described as having 600 wings, blocking the horizon.
  * Contrast them with Jinn, who are made of smokeless fire (*Marij min Nar*) and do have free will to choose between good and evil. (Iblis was a Jinn, not a fallen angel, in Sunni theology).

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 10: The Major Angels and Their Duties
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 10: The Major Angels and Their Duties
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Four columns or cards, each representing one of the major angels with their primary responsibility listed below.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Jibril (جِبْرِيل):** The Archangel of Revelation (*Wahy*). Delivered scripture to the Prophets.
  * **Mika'il (مِيكَائِيل):** Responsible for rain, vegetation, and distributing sustenance (*Rizq*) by Allah's command.
  * **Israfil (إِسْرَافِيل):** The blower of the Trumpet (*Sur*) to signal the end of the world and the Day of Resurrection.
  * **Malik al-Mawt (مَلَكُ الْمَوْت):** The Angel of Death (often named *'Izra'il* in tradition) who extracts souls when their time ends.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Emphasize that these angels do not act independently; they are perfectly organized soldiers executing the orders of Allah.
  * Discuss how *Mika'il* is associated with mercy because rain brings life to dry land, showing Allah's care for all living things.
  * Clarify that the name *'Izra'il* is popular in Islamic literature and cultural tradition, but in the Quran, he is referred to as *Malik al-Mawt* (The Angel of Death). Both are acceptable to mention.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 11: The Angels Who Accompany Us
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 11: The Angels Who Accompany Us
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An illustration of a child walking, with two soft light shapes on either side representing the recording angels, and others around them for protection.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Kiraman Katibin (كِرَامًا كَاتِبِينَ) - The Honorable Recorders:**
    * Two angels sit on our shoulders to write down our deeds.
    * The angel on the right writes good deeds immediately.
    * The angel on the left writes bad deeds, but delays writing to give us time to repent (*Tawbah*).
  * **Al-Hafazah (الْحَفَظَة) - The Protectors:**
    * Guardian angels that protect us from accidents and harm, unless Allah decrees that something should happen.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * In literature, the recording angels are sometimes referred to as *Raqib* (رَقِيب - Watcher) and *'Atid* (عَتِيد - Ready). In Ash'ari theology, these are descriptions of their qualities (that they are always present and ready to record), rather than their unique names.
  * Tell the students the beautiful mercy of the left-shoulder angel: Hadith reports that when a Muslim does a bad deed, the angel on the left raises his pen for a few hours. If the person asks Allah for forgiveness, nothing is written down!

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 12: The Holy Books (Kutub) and the Divine Speech (Kalam)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 12: The Holy Books (Kutub) and the Divine Speech (Kalam)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Images representing scrolls and books. Text highlighting the names of the books and the prophets who received them.
* **Slide Content:**
  * We believe in the original scriptures sent by Allah:
    * **Suhuf (صُحُف):** Scrolls of Ibrahim (Abraham).
    * **Tawrah (تَوْرَاة):** Torah of Musa (Moses).
    * **Zabur (زَبُور):** Psalms of Dawud (David).
    * **Injil (إِنْجِيل):** Gospel of 'Isa (Jesus).
    * **Quran (قُرْآن):** Final Revelation to Muhammad ﷺ.
  * **Ash'ari Theological Distinction:**
    * **Kalam Nafsi (كَلَام نَفْسِي):** Allah's eternal, inner attribute of Speech, which has no letters, sounds, or language.
    * The physical Quran we hold, read, and hear consists of created letters and sounds that *point to* that uncreated Divine Speech.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain the historical context: Sunni scholars had a major debate about whether the Quran is created or uncreated. 
  * The Ash'ari school resolved this with a beautiful distinction: Allah's attribute of Speech (*Kalam*) is eternal and uncreated, just like His Knowledge. However, the Arabic words we print on paper, the sound waves created when we recite, and the ink we use are created things. We must respect the printed Quran because of what it represents—the eternal Speech of Allah.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 13: Prophets and Messengers (Anbiya' and Rusul)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 13: Prophets and Messengers (Anbiya' and Rusul)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A chain link timeline showing the continuity of Prophets from Adam to Muhammad ﷺ, emphasizing they all brought the same message of Tawhid.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Nabi (نَبِي) - Prophet:** A man chosen by Allah to receive guidance, usually following an existing law (*Shari'ah*).
  * **Rasul (رَسُول) - Messenger:** A Prophet who is given a *new* book or a new set of laws (*Shari'ah*).
  * Every *Rasul* is a *Nabi*, but not every *Nabi* is a *Rasul*.
  * Total number: Tens of thousands of Prophets were sent, but **25 are mentioned by name** in the Quran.
  * Core message: Worship Allah alone and do good deeds.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Ask students to name some of the 25 Prophets in the Quran (e.g., Adam, Nuh, Ibrahim, Ismail, Ishaq, Ya'qub, Yusuf, Ayub, Musa, Harun, Dawud, Sulayman, Yunus, Zakariyyah, Yahya, 'Isa, Muhammad).
  * Explain that belief in all Prophets is an all-or-nothing pillar. We cannot believe in Muhammad ﷺ but reject Musa or 'Isa; rejecting one Prophet is like rejecting all of them.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 14: The Infallibility of the Prophets ('Ismah)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 14: The Infallibility of the Prophets ('Ismah)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Icons representing clean virtues: Truth, Trust, Intelligence, and a shield representing protection from sin.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **'Ismah (عِصْمَة):** Infallibility. The protection of Prophets from committing sins.
  * Ash'ari theology states that Prophets are protected from:
    * Major sins (*Kaba'ir*).
    * Minor sins that show a lack of character or base behavior.
    * Lying or breaking promises.
  * Four necessary qualities of every Prophet:
    1. **Sidq (صِدْق):** Complete truthfulness.
    2. **Amanah (أَمَانَة):** Absolute trustworthiness.
    3. **Tabligh (تَبْلِيغ):** Delivering the message without hiding anything.
    4. **Fatanah (فَطَانَة):** Sharp intellect and wisdom.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Why must Prophets be infallible? Because they are our ultimate role models. If they committed sins (like stealing or lying), then Allah would be commanding us to follow people who do bad things, which is logically impossible for the Just Creator.
  * Sometimes the Quran describes a Prophet making a mistake (like Prophet Yunus leaving his people early). Ash'ari scholars explain that these were not *sins* but choices between two good options where they chose the less optimal one, or small slips of judgment (*Zallah*) that Allah corrected immediately to teach humanity.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 15: Believing in Qadar (Divine Decree)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 15: Believing in Qadar (Divine Decree)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An image of a pen writing on a scroll, representing the *Lawh al-Mahfuz* (Preserved Tablet).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Qadar (قَدَر):** Allah's eternal measurement and decree of all things.
  * Four aspects of Qadar (often called the stages of decree):
    1. **'Ilm (Knowledge):** Allah knows everything eternally.
    2. **Kitabah (Writing):** Allah ordered the Pen (*Al-Qalam*) to write everything that will happen in the Preserved Tablet (*Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*).
    3. **Mashi'ah (Will):** Everything happens only if Allah wills it.
    4. **Khalq (Creation):** Allah is the sole Creator of all things, including actions.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Introduce the concept of the *Lawh al-Mahfuz* (اللَّوْح الْمَحْفُوظ). Clarify that the "writing" of the decree does not mean we are forced to do things we don't want to do. The Pen wrote what we *would choose* to do, based on Allah's eternal knowledge.
  * Explain that Qadar is a source of peace for a believer. When something bad happens that is out of our control (like a natural storm or getting sick), we know it was decreed, and we say, *Qaddarallahu wa ma sha'a fa'ala* (Allah has decreed, and what He wills, He does).

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 16: Human Choice and the Ash'ari Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 16: Human Choice and the Ash'ari Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A user interface metaphor: Allah creates the computer system and the keyboard (Power/Creation), but the human chooses which buttons to press (Acquisition).
* **Slide Content:**
  * If Allah creates everything, who is responsible for our actions?
  * **The Ash'ari Answer: Kasb (كَسْب) - Acquisition.**
    * **Creation (Khalq):** Allah creates the ability and the physical action.
    * **Acquisition (Kasb):** The human directs their intention and choice toward that action.
  * *Example:* You decide to give charity. Allah creates the movement of your hand and the money. You "acquire" the deed because you intended and chose to do it.
  * *"For it (the soul) is what it earned (Kasabat), and against it is what it accrued."* (Surah al-Baqarah, 2:286)
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * This is one of the most famous theological debates in Islamic history.
  * Contrast the Ash'ari view with two extremes:
    1. *Jabriyyah* (Determinists): They believed humans have no choice at all, like feathers in the wind. (Rejected!)
    2. *Mu'tazilah* (Rationalists): They believed humans create their own actions independently of Allah. (Rejected!)
  * The Ash'ari middle path is *Kasb*: Allah is the only Creator of effects, but humans are responsible because they have the freedom to intend and choose.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 17: Qadar is Not an Excuse for Bad Choices!
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 17: Qadar is Not an Excuse for Bad Choices!
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A stop sign or warning icon. Side-by-side text contrasting "Excusing choices" vs. "Taking responsibility."
* **Slide Content:**
  * **We cannot use Qadar to justify our sins!**
  * If someone steals money and says, *"It was written in my Qadar, so don't blame me!"* - this is a misuse of belief.
  * **The Law School Analogy:**
    * If you skip studying and fail an exam, you cannot blame the teacher for writing "Fail" on your report card. You made the choice to skip studying.
  * **Use Qadar for comfort in calamity, not as an excuse for laziness or sin.**
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Share the famous story of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab: A thief was brought to him and said, "I only stole because it was decreed by Allah." 'Umar replied, "And we only cut off your hand because it was decreed by Allah!" This shows that Qadar does not bypass justice or accountability.
  * Teach students that we only look at Qadar *after* something happens (to accept it with patience), never *before* it happens (as an excuse to do wrong).

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 18: Why We Learn Schools of Thought (Madhhabs)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 18: Why We Learn Schools of Thought (Madhhabs)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A map of the Muslim world showing different colors for different schools, or a tree with different branches showing unity in the trunk.
* **Slide Content:**
  * Why do different scholars have different opinions on small details?
  * **What is a Madhhab (مَذْهَب)?** A systematic method of understanding the Quran and Sunnah.
  * The four major Sunni schools of law:
    * **Hanafi** (حَنَفِي)
    * **Maliki** (مَالِكِي)
    * **Shafi'i** (شَافِعِي)
    * **Hanbali** (حَنْبَلِي)
  * They agree on 99% of the core of Islam. Their differences are in the secondary details of practice.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that the founders of these schools were great Imams who loved and respected each other. Imam Shafi'i was a student of Imam Malik, and Imam Ahmad was a student of Imam Shafi'i.
  * Reiterate that having a Madhhab is like having a guide who has mapped out the mountain. It is safer to follow an expert map than trying to climb without any training.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 19: The Maliki Madhhab: The Practice of Madinah and Sadl
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 19: The Maliki Madhhab: The Practice of Madinah and Sadl
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** An illustration of a person praying with their hands resting naturally at their sides (*Sadl*), contrasted with hands folded on the chest (*Qabd*).
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Imam Malik ibn Anas (d. 179 AH):** The Imam of Madinah, the city of the Prophet ﷺ.
  * **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah (عَمَل أَهْل الْمَدِينَة):**
    * Imam Malik looked at how the children and grandchildren of the Sahabah in Madinah practiced Islam as a living proof of the Sunnah.
  * **Sadl (سَدْل) vs. Qabd (قَبْض) in Salah:**
    * **Sadl:** Praying with arms hanging naturally at the sides. This is the preferred position in fard (obligatory) prayers in the Maliki school.
    * Why? Because Imam Malik observed the people of Madinah praying this way.
    * Both Sadl and Qabd are valid Sunni practices.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Address a common point of confusion for kids: "Why does that person pray differently?" 
  * Explain that in the Maliki school, *Sadl* is the primary position because it was the continuous, public practice of the city of Madinah. If the Prophet ﷺ had ordered everyone to fold their hands, the entire city of Madinah would not have agreed on praying with their hands down. Therefore, it is a highly respected Sunnah.
  * Note: In Maliki fiqh, it is also permitted to fold hands (*Qabd*) in nafl (voluntary) prayers, but *Sadl* is preferred in fard prayers.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 20: More Maliki Rulings on Salah
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 20: More Maliki Rulings on Salah
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Checklist format detailing specific Maliki rulings on Salah.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Recitation of the Basmalah (بِسْمِ اللّٰهِ الرَّحْمٰنِ الرَّحِيمِ):**
    * In the Maliki school, we do not recite the *Basmalah* aloud or silently before Al-Fatihah in the fard prayers. We start directly with *"Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'Alamin."*
  * **Making Sujud al-Sahw (Prostration of Forgetfulness):**
    * **Ba'di (بَعْدِي - After):** If you added something extra to the prayer by mistake, you make sujud *after* the Taslim.
    * **Qabli (قَبْلِي - Before):** If you missed a sunnah act in the prayer, you make sujud *before* the Taslim.
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Explain that not reciting the *Basmalah* in fard prayers is another practice of the people of Madinah. Malikis believe Al-Fatihah is the start of the recitation, and the Basmalah is a separator between Surahs, not a verse of Al-Fatihah itself.
  * Introduce *Sujud al-Sahw* (سُجُود السَّهْو) simply. The distinction between *Qabli* (before Taslim for omission) and *Ba'di* (after Taslim for addition) is a beautiful, logical system unique to the Maliki school.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 21: Summary & Reflection
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 21: Summary & Reflection
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** Summary list on the left, a thought-bubble illustration with the word "Reflection" on the right.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **What we have learned today:**
    * Allah is Unique and not like His creation (*Mukhalafah*).
    * The Six Pillars of Iman anchor our hearts.
    * Angels surround us, recording deeds and protecting us.
    * Qadar is Allah's decree, but we are responsible for our choices (*Kasb*).
    * Scholar differences, like *Sadl* in Maliki fiqh, are a mercy.
  * **Reflection Question:**
    * *How does knowing that Allah creates our physical abilities, but we choose how to use them (Kasb), change the way you think about your daily choices?*
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Conclude the lesson by asking the students to sit quietly for two minutes to think about the reflection question.
  * Invite two or three students to share their answers. Emphasize that every choice we make (e.g., helping a friend, studying, speaking kindly) is a physical movement created by Allah, but our soul is what decided to do it, and that is what Allah rewards.

---

parsedSlides.title: Slide 22: Sources & References (For Teachers)
parsedSlides.content:
## Slide 22: Sources & References (For Teachers)
* **Visual Guide / Layout:** A academic-looking bibliography slide with book covers or text styling.
* **Slide Content:**
  * **Aqidah (Ash'ari School):**
    * *Al-Aqidah al-Sanusiyyah* (Umm al-Barahin) by Imam Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sanusi.
    * *Jawharat al-Tawhid* by Imam Ibrahim al-Laqani.
  * **Fiqh (Maliki School):**
    * *Al-Muwatta* of Imam Malik ibn Anas.
    * *Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah* by Imam Abd al-Bari al-'Ashmawi.
    * *Risalah* of Imam Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani (d. 386 AH).
  * **Hadith & Creed:**
    * *Sahih al-Bukhari* & *Sahih Muslim* (Hadith of Jibril).
* **Teacher Notes:**
  * Encourage parents/teachers to reference these classical texts if they want to study deeper.
  * The *Risalah* of Ibn Abi Zayd is a standard manual for Maliki fiqh and contains a beautiful introduction to Sunni/Ash'ari Aqidah, perfect for students.

# Voice Script: Foundations of Belief
**Topic:** Who is Allah? Names and Attributes, Pillars of Iman, Angels, Holy Books & Prophets, Qadar, and Maliki/Ash'ari Literacy.  
**Audience:** Parents/Teachers presenting to children aged 10–13.  
**Creed/Law Framework:** Ash'ari Aqidah & Maliki Fiqh.  
**Model Tuning:** ElevenLabs v3 with native expressive audio tags ([warmly], [thoughtful], [reverent], [pause], [short pause]).

---

## Slide 1: Islamic Creed (Aqidah) & Law (Fiqh) for Teachers
* **Slide Summary:** Course title and opening orientation covering Aqidah, Fiqh, the Pillars of Iman, and classical scholarship.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with warmth, welcome, and inspiring energy to set a welcoming tone for teachers, parents, and students]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[warmly] Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim. [pause] Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh. [pause] Welcome to our foundational journey through Islamic Creed—[short pause]*Aqidah*—and Islamic Law—[short pause]*Fiqh*. [long pause] In this unit, we will explore the most profound questions of our existence: [short pause] Who is Allah? [short pause] How do we understand His Beautiful Names and Necessary Attributes? [pause] What are the Six Pillars of Iman? [pause] How do Angels, Divine Books, Prophets, and the mystery of Divine Decree—*Qadar*—shape our worldview? [long pause] Together, we will examine these sacred truths through the authentic, time-tested scholarship of the Ash'ari school of creed and the Maliki school of jurisprudence. [pause] Let us begin with open minds and receptive hearts."
* **Concept Analogy:** A compass and a map: Aqidah is our spiritual compass that points our hearts to Allah, while Fiqh is the map showing us each practical step of the road.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What two foundational branches of Islamic knowledge are we exploring in this course?"

---

## Slide 2: Introduction to Aqidah & Fiqh
* **Slide Summary:** Definitions of Aqidah and Fiqh, and why we study classical Madhhabs.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Smile, engage the audience directly, and use clear contrast gestures]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[welcoming] Assalamu Alaikum, everyone! Welcome! [pause] Today, we begin by looking at the two essential dimensions of our faith: [short pause] **Aqidah** and **Fiqh**. [pause] Think of *Aqidah* as the roots of a mighty tree. [short pause] You cannot see the roots, but they anchor the tree deep into the earth. [pause] *Aqidah* is what we believe with certainty in our hearts—[short pause]our conviction about Allah, His Angels, and the unseen realm. [long pause] *Fiqh*, on the other hand, is like the trunk, branches, leaves, and sweet fruit of that tree. [pause] It is the practical guide for *how* we live—[short pause]how we perform Wudu, [short pause]how we offer Salah, [short pause]and how we treat our families and communities. [long pause] In this series, we learn through the lens of two classical schools of thought: [short pause] the **Ash'ari** school of creed, [short pause] and the **Maliki** school of law. [pause] Why do we follow a systematic school—a *Madhhab*? [short pause] Because it builds deep theological literacy, [short pause] and teaches us to appreciate the rich, brilliant heritage of Islamic scholarship across centuries."
* **Concept Analogy:** A fruit tree: Aqidah is the hidden, nourishing root system, while Fiqh is the visible, flourishing branches bearing good deeds.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "If I believe in Angels with all my heart, is that an example of Aqidah or Fiqh? What about learning how to pray?"

---

## Slide 3: Who is Allah? The Core Principle of Tawhid
* **Slide Summary:** Core principles of Tawhid, and the divine names Al-Wahid and Al-Ahad.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Lower voice pitch slightly to inspire awe and reverence; articulate deliberately]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[reverent, awe] Let us ask the most important question in the entire universe: [pause] *Who is Allah?* [long pause] The answer is captured in one monumental word: [short pause] **Tawheed**. [pause] Tawheed is the uncompromising, absolute belief that Allah is One. [pause] He is **Al-Waahid** and **Al-Ahad**—[short pause]The Singular, the Unique, the Absolutely Indivisible. [pause] He has no partners, [short pause] no parents, [short pause] no children, [short pause] and no equals whatsoever. [long pause] In the Ash'ari school of theology, scholars emphasize that the very first obligation—*the first Wajib*—upon any Muslim who reaches maturity is to know Allah. [pause] Not merely by memorizing phrases, [short pause] but by reflecting deeply upon creation, using our God-given intellect to recognize the magnificent Creator behind it all."
* **Concept Analogy:** A masterpiece painting or an intricate watch: just by observing the precision and beauty, you instantly know an intelligent designer made it, even if you cannot see them.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What Surah in the Quran is considered the ultimate summary of Tawhid? (Answer: Surah al-Ikhlas)."

---

## Slide 4: Knowing Allah through His Necessary Attributes (Sifat al-Wajibah)
* **Slide Summary:** Understanding the 20 necessary attributes of Allah across four categories (Nafsiyyah, Salbiyyah, Ma'ani, and Ma'nawiyyah).
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with structured clarity; count categories cleanly]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[methodical, clear] To truly know Allah, scholars organized what the Quran and reason teach us into twenty necessary attributes, called **Sifaat al-Waajibah**. [pause] In Ash'ari creed, these twenty attributes are arranged into four clear groups. [pause] First: **Nafsiyyah**—the Personal Attribute, which is **Wujud**—the eternal Existence of Allah. [pause] Second: **Salbiyyah**—the Negative or Exclusionary attributes, which negate any flaw from Allah. [short pause] These include His beginninglessness (*Qidam*), [short pause] His endlessness (*Baqa'*), [short pause] His absolute difference from creation (*Mukhalafah*), [short pause] His self-subsistence (*Qiyam bi-Nafsih*), [short pause] and His absolute Oneness (*Wahdaniyyah*). [long pause] Third: **Sifaat al-Ma'ani**—the Qualitative attributes. [short pause] These are Allah's Divine Power (*Qudrah*), [short pause] Will (*Iradah*), [short pause] Knowledge (*'Ilm*), [short pause] Life (*Hayat*), [short pause] Hearing (*Sam'*), [short pause] Sight (*Basar*), [short pause] and Divine Speech (*Kalam*). [long pause] And fourth: **Sifaat al-Ma'nawiyyah**—the Active State attributes, [short pause] meaning that Allah is perpetually and actively Powerful, [short pause] Willful, [short pause] Knowing, [short pause] Living, [short pause] Hearing, [short pause] Seeing, [short pause] and Speaking. [pause] Remember: [short pause] Allah's hearing and seeing are not like ours. [short pause] He does not need ears, eyes, or instruments. [short pause] His attributes are perfect, eternal, and without limits."
* **Concept Analogy:** Our vision requires light, eyes, and distance. Allah's sight encompasses every atom in total darkness without any organ or limitation.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What are the four categories of the 20 necessary attributes in Ash'ari creed? (Answer: Nafsiyyah, Salbiyyah, Ma'ani, and Ma'nawiyyah)."

---

## Slide 5: Transcending Space and Time (Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith)
* **Slide Summary:** Declaring Allah free of any resemblance to created things (Tanzih).
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Use open, expansive hand gestures; speak with conviction]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[firm, inspiring] This leads us to one of the most foundational principles in Sunni theology: [short pause] **Mukhaalafah lil-Hawaadith**. [pause] This means that Allah is completely, utterly different from created things. [pause] Allah is not a physical body—[short pause]He is not a *Jirm*. [short pause] He does not occupy physical space, [short pause] nor is He located in a direction. [pause] Why? [short pause] Because Allah is the Creator of space, and He is the Creator of time! [pause] Since He created them, He cannot be bounded or trapped inside them. [long pause] As Allah states clearly in Surah ash-Shura: [short pause] *Laysa kamithlihi shay'un*—[short pause]'There is nothing like unto Him.' [long pause] Our classical Imams left us a golden rule to remember: [short pause] Whatever image or concept crosses your human mind, [short pause] Allah is completely different from that."
* **Concept Analogy:** A software engineer who codes a 3D video game. The coder does not live inside the pixels of the computer monitor; they exist entirely outside the physical rules of the game they built.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "Why can't Allah be contained within space or time? (Answer: Because He created space and time, and the Creator is not contained by His creation)."

---

## Slide 6: The Names of Allah (Al-Asma' al-Husna)
* **Slide Summary:** The 99 Beautiful Names of Allah and their active role in a Muslim's spiritual life.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with heartfelt warmth and personal resonance]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[tender, heartfelt] Allah has made Himself known to us through His most beautiful names: [short pause] **Al-Asma' al-Husna**. [pause] The Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, taught us in Sahih al-Bukhari: [short pause] 'Allah has ninety-nine names, one hundred less one. [short pause] Whoever guards and lives by them will enter Paradise.' [long pause] Guarding them does not mean merely reciting them like a list. [pause] It means understanding how Allah manifests His care and majesty in our lives. [pause] When you feel down or make a mistake, [short pause] you call upon **Al-Ghaffar**—The Repeatedly Forgiving. [pause] When you need sustenance, health, or success in school, [short pause] you beseech **Al-Razzaq**—The Supreme Provider. [pause] When life feels confusing, [short pause] you trust in **Al-Hakim**—The Perfectly Wise. [pause] Every name is a doorway to love, awe, and intimate connection with your Lord."
* **Concept Analogy:** Knowing someone's name and character unlocks friendship; knowing Allah's names unlocks true love and reliance on Him.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "Which Name of Allah would you call upon when you feel nervous and need protection? (e.g., Al-Hafiz, The Protector)."

---

## Slide 7: Ash'ari Reading of Sacred Texts: Tafwid and Ta'wil
* **Slide Summary:** How Sunni scholarship approaches apparent anthropomorphic verses without compromising transcendence.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Adopt an intellectual, reassuring tone; illustrate balance]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[scholarly, thoughtful] In the Quran, we sometimes encounter phrases like the 'Hand'—*Yad*—of Allah, [short pause] the 'Face'—*Wajh*—of Allah, [short pause] or Allah 'establishing' over the Throne—*Al-Istiwa'*. [pause] Since we know beyond doubt that Allah is free from having a physical body or human parts, [short pause] how do orthodox Sunni scholars read these texts? [long pause] They follow two valid, noble methodologies: [pause] First: **Tafweed**—the way of the early generations, the *Salaf*. [short pause] In Tafweed, we affirm the sacred wording as revealed, [short pause] we strip away any physical or bodily meaning, [short pause] and we say: 'Allah knows best the true reality of His words.' [long pause] Second: **Ta'weel**—the method formalized by later scholars, the *Khalaf*. [short pause] Ta'weel provides a figurative, metaphorical interpretation consistent with classical Arabic language. [pause] For example: [short pause] 'Hand' is understood as Divine Power (*Qudrah*) or Divine Generosity (*Ni'mah*). [pause] And *Istiwa'* over the Throne is understood as Supreme Sovereignty and Control (*Istila'*). [pause] Both Tafweed and Ta'weel share the exact same foundation: [short pause] they completely protect our belief from *Tashbeeh*—[short pause]the error of comparing Allah to human beings."
* **Concept Analogy:** When someone says, 'Could you lend me a hand?', you don't expect them to literally cut off their hand; you know from language that they are offering help.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What do both Tafwid and Ta'wil agree on? (Answer: That Allah does not have a physical body, limbs, or human qualities)."

---

## Slide 8: The Six Pillars of Iman (Overview)
* **Slide Summary:** Overview of the Six Pillars of Faith as established in the Hadith of Jibril.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with structured enthusiasm; establish a clear roadmap]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[structured, enthusiastic] Now let us turn to the structural foundation of our inner religion: [short pause] the **Six Pillars of Iman**. [pause] In the renowned Hadith of Jibril, [short pause] the Archangel Jibril came in the form of a traveler in pure white garments to question the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in front of the Companions. [pause] When asked, 'What is Iman?', [short pause] the Messenger of Allah replied that faith is to firmly believe in six truths: [pause] One: **Allah**. [short pause] Two: **His Angels**. [short pause] Three: **His Revealed Scriptures**. [short pause] Four: **His Messengers**. [short pause] Five: **The Last Day**. [short pause] And six: **Divine Decree—Qadar**—both its sweet and its bitter. [long pause] Notice the crucial distinction: [short pause] *Islam* refers to our outer, physical acts of obedience—like praying and fasting. [pause] *Iman* refers to the unshakable conviction anchored deep within our hearts."
* **Concept Analogy:** A magnificent palace: the pillars hold up the entire ceiling. If even one pillar is removed, the structural integrity of the roof is lost.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What is the primary difference between Islam and Iman? (Answer: Islam is outward submission and practice; Iman is inward conviction and belief)."

---

## Slide 9: Iman in Allah and His Attributes of Power, Will, and Knowledge
* **Slide Summary:** The theological interplay between Divine Knowledge, Divine Will, and Divine Power.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Use harmonious hand motions to depict three gears turning in concert]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[deeply reflective] In Ash'ari Aqidah, three central divine attributes help us understand how Allah acts within our universe: [pause] Knowledge, [short pause] Will, [short pause] and Power. [long pause] First: **Al-'Ilm**—Divine Knowledge. [short pause] Allah knows everything that was, [short pause] everything that is, [short pause] and everything that will ever be, [short pause] eternally and without learning. [pause] Second: **Al-Iradah**—Divine Will. [short pause] Allah specifies which possibilities happen, [short pause] choosing exact timings, forms, and conditions. [pause] Third: **Al-Qudrah**—Divine Power. [short pause] Allah brings those willed possibilities from non-existence into real existence. [long pause] Reflect on a single autumn leaf fluttering from an oak tree. [pause] Allah's *'Ilm* eternally knew that leaf would fall at precisely three seconds past noon. [pause] His *Iradah* specified that it should fall at that exact second rather than any other. [pause] And His *Qudrah* exercised the power that detached the leaf and guided it gracefully to the earth. [pause] Nothing in existence escapes this divine harmony."
* **Concept Analogy:** An architect: they understand the master blueprint (Knowledge), they decide when to begin construction (Will), and they deploy the resources to build the structure (Power).
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "Does Allah ever learn new information as events unfold? (Answer: No, His Knowledge is eternal, perfect, and all-encompassing)."

---

## Slide 10: Angels: Creation, Nature, and Characteristics
* **Slide Summary:** The creation of Angels from light, their lack of gender and biological needs, and their sinless obedience.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with serene wonder and reverence]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[serene, wondrous] Now we arrive at the second pillar of faith: [short pause] **Angels**—*Mala'ikah*. [pause] Angels are noble, luminous creations of Allah, crafted from pure light—*Nur*. [pause] They are completely different from human beings. [short pause] They have no physical gender—[short pause]they are neither male nor female. [short pause] They do not eat, [short pause] they do not drink, [short pause] they do not sleep, [short pause] and they never grow weary or tired. [long pause] Crucially, angels do not possess human free will. [short pause] They cannot choose to rebel or disobey their Lord. [pause] As Allah describes them in Surah at-Tahrim: [short pause] 'They do not disobey Allah in whatever He commands them, [short pause] and they carry out exactly what they are ordered.' [pause] Their entire existence is perpetual praise, service, and flawless execution of the divine decree."
* **Concept Analogy:** Like the planets revolving flawlessly along their orbital paths without ever veering, angels fulfill Allah's commands with absolute precision.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "Is Iblis (Satan) an angel who fell from grace in Islamic belief? (Answer: No, Iblis is from the Jinn, created from smokeless fire, and he possessed free will)."

---

## Slide 11: The Major Angels and Their Duties
* **Slide Summary:** Roles of the four archangels: Jibril, Mika'il, Israfil, and Malik al-Mawt.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Articulate each archangel's name distinctly; use deliberate pacing]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[deliberate, solemn] While Allah created uncounted legions of angels, [short pause] revelation introduces us to four supreme Archangels, each entrusted with a vital cosmic mission. [long pause] First: **Jibreel**—the Archangel of Revelation—*Wahy*. [short pause] Jibreel conveyed the sacred words of Allah to the hearts of all the Prophets. [pause] Second: **Mika'eel**—responsible for the elements, [short pause] rain, [short pause] the nourishment of crops, [short pause] and the distribution of sustenance—*Rizq*—by Allah's permission. [pause] Third: **Israfeel**—the blower of the mighty Trumpet—*As-Soor*. [short pause] Israfeel stands poised, awaiting the divine command to blow the blast that ends this world, [short pause] and the second blast that initiates the Day of Resurrection. [long pause] And fourth: **Malik al-Mawt**—the Angel of Death. [short pause] Entrusted with taking the souls of creation when their appointed lifespan on this earth has reached its final second. [pause] They operate with majestic order, [short pause] carrying out the will of Allah across the cosmos."
* **Concept Analogy:** High commissioners in a kingdom: each leader is entrusted with a distinct domain—communication, agriculture, timekeeping, and border transitions.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What is the Quranic title of the Angel of Death? (Answer: Malik al-Mawt)."

---

## Slide 12: The Angels Who Accompany Us
* **Slide Summary:** Understanding the Kiraman Katibin (Recorders) and Al-Hafazah (Protectors).
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak in a comforting, intimate tone; gesture toward the shoulders]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[gentle, comforting] Did you know that you are accompanied by angels this very second? [pause] Assigned to each of us are the **Kiraaman Kaatibeen**—the Honorable Recorders. [pause] Two noble angels sit beside our shoulders. [short pause] The angel on our right immediately records every good deed, every kind word, and every sincere smile. [pause] The angel on our left records bad deeds. [short pause] But observe the breathtaking mercy of our Creator: [short pause] the left angel pauses and delays writing for a period of hours. [pause] If you feel regret, make Tawbah, and say *Astaghfirullah*, [short pause] that angel drops the pen, and nothing is written in your book! [long pause] Beside them walk **Al-Hafadhah**—the Guardian Angels. [short pause] They shield us from unseen hazards, illnesses, and harm throughout our days and nights, [short pause] stepping aside only when Allah decrees a test for our spiritual growth. [pause] A believer is never abandoned, and never alone."
* **Concept Analogy:** A continuous recording journal where every positive accomplishment is locked in immediately, while errors can be deleted and cleared before they are finalized.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What happens to a bad deed if a believer immediately repents and asks for forgiveness? (Answer: The angel on the left does not record it)."

---

## Slide 13: The Holy Books (Kutub) and the Divine Speech (Kalam)
* **Slide Summary:** The revealed scriptures and the Ash'ari distinction between Kalam Nafsi and Kalam Lafzi.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with dignity; pause deliberately before theological distinctions]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[dignified, profound] The third pillar of Iman is belief in the **Holy Books**—*Al-Kutub*. [pause] We believe in the original divine revelations bestowed upon the Prophets: [short pause] The *Suhuf* granted to Ibrahim; [short pause] the *Tawrah* revealed to Musa; [short pause] the *Zabur* given to Dawud; [short pause] the *Injil* sent to 'Isa; [short pause] and the final, incorruptible revelation—the *Quran*—revealed to Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. [long pause] Ash'ari scholarship draws a profound theological distinction regarding Divine Speech: [pause] Allah's eternal attribute of speech is called **Kalam Nafsi**—[short pause]His intrinsic, eternal Speech, which exists without sounds, syllables, or letters. [pause] The physical Arabic Quran that we recite with our tongues, hear with our ears, and touch on paper consists of **Kalam Lafzi**—[short pause]created sounds and letters that signify and point to that uncreated Divine Speech. [pause] We revere and sanctify the physical Mushaf because it manifests and conveys the eternal guidance of our Lord."
* **Concept Analogy:** An unexpressed thought in your heart: it possesses meaning without ink or sound. When you write it into a letter, you use created ink and letters to convey that meaning to the world.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What is the difference between Kalam Nafsi and Kalam Lafzi in Ash'ari theology?"

---

## Slide 14: Prophets and Messengers (Anbiya' and Rusul)
* **Slide Summary:** Distinguishing between Nabi and Rasul, total numbers, and their unified message.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with warmth and deep admiration for the prophetic lineage]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[warm, admiring] Our fourth pillar is belief in the **Prophets and Messengers**—*Al-Anbiya' wal-Rusul*. [pause] Is there a difference between a *Nabi* and a *Rasul*? [pause] Yes, classical scholarship explains that a **Nabi** is an inspired Prophet chosen by Allah to receive divine guidance and invite people to follow an existing sacred law—*Shari'ah*. [pause] A **Rasul** is a Messenger who is given a new book or a distinct divine legal code. [pause] Therefore, [short pause] every Rasul is a Nabi, [short pause] but not every Nabi is a Rasul. [long pause] Over human history, Allah dispatched over one hundred thousand prophets, [short pause] and twenty-five of them are named specifically in the Holy Quran. [pause] From Adam to Nuh, [short pause] from Ibrahim to Musa, [short pause] from 'Isa to Muhammad, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, [short pause] they all delivered one unified message: [short pause] 'Worship Allah alone without partners, [short pause] and live with righteousness and justice.'"
* **Concept Analogy:** In education, every school principal is a certified teacher, but not every teacher is a principal tasked with introducing a school-wide curriculum.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "How many Prophets are mentioned by name in the Quran? (Answer: 25 Prophets)."

---

## Slide 15: The Infallibility of the Prophets ('Ismah)
* **Slide Summary:** Infallibility ('Ismah) and the four necessary character traits of every Prophet.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with moral clarity and authoritative confidence]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[authoritative, upright] Because the Prophets were sent as humanity's moral exemplars, [short pause] Allah granted them divine protection called **'Ismah**—Infallibility. [pause] In Ash'ari theology, Prophets are absolutely protected from committing major sins, [short pause] protected from minor sins that imply baseness or dishonor, [short pause] and protected from ever lying or breaking a promise. [long pause] Scholars identified four necessary attributes that every true Prophet must possess: [pause] One: **Sidq**—unflinching truthfulness. [short pause] Two: **Amanah**—absolute trustworthiness and integrity. [short pause] Three: **Tabligh**—the faithful conveyance of every single message without withholding anything. [short pause] And four: **Fatanah**—sharp intellect, supreme wisdom, and discernment. [long pause] If a Prophet could commit sins, [short pause] then Allah would be commanding us to emulate wrongdoing, which is impossible. [pause] The Prophets are pure, spotless mirrors of divine virtue."
* **Concept Analogy:** A maritime lighthouse: its glass must remain immaculately spotless. If the glass were smeared with mud or cracks, ships navigating stormy waters would be misled into disaster.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "Name the four necessary qualities that every Prophet must possess. (Answer: Sidq, Amanah, Tabligh, and Fatanah)."

---

## Slide 16: Believing in Qadar (Divine Decree)
* **Slide Summary:** Understanding Qadar through its four theological stages: 'Ilm, Kitabah, Mashi'ah, and Khalq.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with a reassuring, grounding cadence]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[calm, grounding] Now we arrive at the sixth pillar of faith: [short pause] belief in **Qadar**—the Divine Decree. [pause] Qadar is the comforting conviction that Allah has measured, planned, and decreed all things with perfect wisdom. [long pause] Classical theology outlines four essential dimensions of Qadar: [pause] First: **Al-'Ilm**—Divine Knowledge. [short pause] Allah knew every occurrence before time began. [pause] Second: **Al-Kitabah**—The Writing. [short pause] Allah commanded the primordial Pen—*Al-Qalam*—to record all that would happen until eternity in the Preserved Tablet—*Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz*. [pause] Third: **Al-Mashi'ah**—The Divine Will. [short pause] Whatever Allah wills comes to pass, [short pause] and whatever He does not will can never happen. [pause] And fourth: **Al-Khalq**—Creation. [short pause] Allah is the sole, ultimate Creator of everything in existence, including actions and causes. [long pause] When a believer absorbs Qadar, anxiety dissolves. [short pause] You realize that what missed you was never meant to strike you, [short pause] and what struck you was never meant to miss you."
* **Concept Analogy:** A master blueprint created by an omniscient architect. No unexpected turn or accident ever catches the designer off guard.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What were the two instruments involved in recording the decree before creation? (Answer: The Pen, Al-Qalam, and the Preserved Tablet, Al-Lawh al-Mahfuz)."

---

## Slide 17: Human Choice and the Ash'ari Concept of Kasb (Acquisition)
* **Slide Summary:** Resolving the relationship between Divine omnipotence and human accountability through Kasb.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Engage the audience intellectually; emphasize the moral responsibility]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[thoughtful, engaging] A crucial question often arises: [short pause] If Allah creates everything, why are we held accountable for our actions? [pause] The Ash'ari tradition provides an elegant, profound answer known as the doctrine of **Kasb**—Acquisition. [long pause] We distinguish between two realities: [pause] **Khalq**—Creation. [short pause] Allah alone creates the physical power, the circumstances, and the bodily movement. [pause] And **Kasb**—Acquisition. [short pause] The human being exercises their intention, willingness, and moral choice to direct that energy toward good or evil. [long pause] Think of giving charity: [short pause] Allah created the money, your arm muscles, and the paper notes. [short pause] But *you* directed your heart and intention to give that money to the poor. [pause] You 'acquired' that moral deed! [pause] This is exactly what Allah declares in Surah al-Baqarah: [short pause] *Laha ma kasabat wa 'alayha maktasabat*—[short pause]'For every soul is the good it acquired, [short pause] and against it is the evil it accrued.' [pause] We are rewarded and held accountable based on the choices of our hearts."
* **Concept Analogy:** A driver behind the steering wheel of an automobile: the manufacturer engineered the engine, wheels, and fuel, but the driver decides whether to steer toward safety or off the road.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What is the difference between Khalq and Kasb? (Answer: Khalq is Allah creating the power and action; Kasb is the human acquiring the deed through intention and choice)."

---

## Slide 18: Qadar is Not an Excuse for Bad Choices!
* **Slide Summary:** Refuting the fatalistic excuse of using Qadar to justify negligence or sin.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Adopt a firm, practical, and cautionary tone]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[firm, cautionary] We must establish a vital truth: [short pause] *Qadar can never be used as an excuse for bad behavior or sinful choices!* [pause] If a student chooses to play video games all night, ignores their homework, fails an exam, and then declares: [short pause] 'Well, Allah decreed that I would fail'—[short pause]they are completely abusing theology. [pause] They chose not to study! [long pause] Remember the famous encounter during the Caliphate of 'Umar ibn al-Khattab. [short pause] A thief was brought before him and pleaded: [short pause] 'Do not punish me, O Leader of the Believers! I only stole because it was written in my Qadar!' [pause] 'Umar famously replied: [short pause] 'And we are only cutting off your hand by the Qadar of Allah!' [long pause] Here is the golden rule: [short pause] We look back at Qadar *after* hardships strike to find solace, patience, and peace; [pause] we never look forward to Qadar *before* acting as an excuse for laziness or sin."
* **Concept Analogy:** If you purposely jump into a pool wearing a suit, you cannot blame the water for getting you wet; you made the conscious choice to jump in.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "When is it appropriate to reflect on Qadar—before making a moral choice, or after an unavoidable calamity occurs? (Answer: After an outcome occurs, as a source of patience and contentment)."

---

## Slide 19: Why We Learn Schools of Thought (Madhhabs)
* **Slide Summary:** The purpose, scholarly lineage, and legitimacy of the four Sunni legal schools.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with deep respect for intellectual heritage and broad-mindedness]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[appreciative, respectful] Why do qualified scholars sometimes hold differing views on small details of practice? [pause] This brings us to the beauty of **Madhhabs**—our legal schools of thought. [pause] A *Madhhab* is not a separate religion; [short pause] it is a rigorous, systematic methodology for interpreting the Quran and Sunnah. [long pause] Sunni Islam recognizes four great canonical schools of law: [pause] The **Hanafi** school, [short pause] the **Maliki** school, [short pause] the **Shafi'i** school, [short pause] and the **Hanbali** school. [pause] These schools agree on ninety-nine percent of Islamic law! [pause] They agree on the Pillars of Islam, the halal, the haram, and the articles of faith. [pause] Their minor differences lie in secondary operational details. [pause] Their founding Imams loved, studied under, and deeply respected one another. [pause] Learning through a recognized school of thought protects us from personal whim and connects our worship to an unbroken chain of authoritative scholarship."
* **Concept Analogy:** Four medical specialists trained at elite universities: each follows the same science of medicine, but they may offer slightly different, highly valid treatment strategies based on clinical evidence.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What are the four major Sunni schools of jurisprudence? (Answer: Hanafi, Maliki, Shafi'i, and Hanbali)."

---

## Slide 20: The Maliki Madhhab: The Practice of Madinah and Sadl
* **Slide Summary:** Imam Malik ibn Anas, the evidentiary weight of 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah, and the practice of Sadl in prayer.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Demonstrate posture reverently; celebrate scholarly authenticity]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[grounded, authentic] Let us explore the **Maliki school**, [short pause] founded by Imam Malik ibn Anas, who lived in Madinah—the blessed city of the Messenger of Allah, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam. [pause] Imam Malik utilized a profound legal source: [short pause] **'Amal Ahl al-Madinah**—the living, continuous practice of the people of Madinah. [pause] He reasoned that when thousands of children and grandchildren of the Sahabah in Madinah all perform an act of worship in unison, [short pause] that inherited communal practice is a living, mass-transmitted proof of the Sunnah. [long pause] A well-known example of this is **Sadl** in Salah—[short pause]praying with your arms resting naturally at your sides. [pause] In the Maliki school, *Sadl* is the preferred position in obligatory—*Fard*—prayers. [pause] Why? [short pause] Because Imam Malik observed the senior scholars and descendants of the Companions in Madinah standing before Allah in that manner. [pause] Both *Sadl* and *Qabd*—clasping the hands—are authentic, verified Sunni practices. [pause] We respect both without judgment."
* **Concept Analogy:** An unbroken family heirloom recipe handed down directly from mothers and grandmothers in the hometown, verified by hundreds of families cooking it daily.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What is 'Amal Ahl al-Madinah and why did Imam Malik give it such high authority? (Answer: The living continuous practice of the people of Madinah, acting as mass-transmitted living evidence of the Prophet's Sunnah)."

---

## Slide 21: More Maliki Rulings on Salah
* **Slide Summary:** Maliki rulings on beginning Al-Fatihah without vocalizing the Basmalah in Fard prayers, and the structure of Sujud al-Sahw.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with clear, practical instruction; contrast Qabli and Ba'di]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[practical, clear] Let us look at two additional distinctive rulings in Maliki Fiqh that every student should know. [pause] First: **The Recitation of the Basmalah**. [short pause] In the Maliki school, when praying obligatory prayers, [short pause] we do not recite *Bismillahir-Rahmanir-Rahim* aloud or quietly before Surah al-Fatihah. [pause] The Imam begins recitation immediately with: [short pause] *Al-Hamdu lillahi Rabbil-'Alamin*. [pause] This is because in the Maliki tradition, the Basmalah is viewed as a sacred blessing opening the Surah, rather than an integral verse of Al-Fatihah itself. [long pause] Second: **Sujud al-Sahw**—the Prostrations of Forgetfulness. [pause] Maliki fiqh provides an exceptionally clear rule: [pause] If you *omitted* an emphasized sunnah from your prayer, [short pause] you perform two prostrations **Qabli**—[short pause]*before* making the final Taslim. [pause] But if you *added* something extra by mistake, [short pause] you perform two prostrations **Ba'di**—[short pause]*after* completing the Taslim. [pause] It is a remarkably logical, elegant system of worship."
* **Concept Analogy:** A repair manual: if you accidentally forgot a bolt before closing the machine, you insert it before finishing (Qabli); if you ended up with an extra piece on the bench, you address it after the run is complete (Ba'di).
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "If someone accidentally missed reciting the Tashahhud in prayer, do they perform prostrations Qabli or Ba'di? (Answer: Qabli, because a sunnah element was omitted)."

---

## Slide 22: Summary & Reflection
* **Slide Summary:** Comprehensive review of core takeaways and an interactive reflection prompt on Kasb.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with warm summation and reflective sincerity; invite pause and contemplation]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[reflective, warm] SubhanAllah, [short pause] look at the vast expanse of sacred wisdom we have navigated together today! [pause] Let us summarize our key principles: [pause] Allah is One, [short pause] Unique, [short pause] and beyond space and time—*Mukhalafah lil-Hawadith*. [pause] The Six Pillars of Iman anchor our hearts and guide our worldview. [pause] Angels surround us constantly, [short pause] guarding us and faithfully recording our deeds. [pause] Qadar is Allah's perfect decree, [short pause] while our moral choices—*Kasb*—determine our deeds and accountability. [pause] And our Madhhabs, such as the Maliki school, are an ocean of mercy connecting us directly to the Prophetic tradition. [long pause] Now, take a quiet moment to reflect on this question: [pause] *How does knowing that Allah creates all ability, but you choose how to direct it through Kasb, change the way you approach your daily intentions and choices?* [long pause] Take a minute to ponder this in your heart."
* **Delivery Tip:** `[Allow 1-2 minutes of classroom silence, then invite students or family members to share their reflections.]`
* **Concept Analogy:** A completed jigsaw puzzle: each individual piece—Aqidah, the Pillars, the Angels, Qadar, and Fiqh—locks together to reveal a stunning, unified picture of faith and purposeful living.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What is one key lesson you will take away from today's study of Aqidah and Fiqh?"

---

## Slide 23: Sources & References (For Teachers)
* **Slide Summary:** Scholarly academic references in Ash'ari Aqidah, Maliki Fiqh, and Hadith for educators and parents.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Address teachers and parents with professional, scholarly respect]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[professional, respectful] To our dedicated teachers and parents: [pause] the foundations taught in this lesson are rooted in the classical canons of orthodox Sunni scholarship. [long pause] For **Ash'ari Aqidah**, [short pause] we rely upon *Al-Aqidah al-Sanusiyyah*—known as *Umm al-Barahin*—by Imam Muhammad ibn Yusuf al-Sanusi, [short pause] and *Jawharat al-Tawhid* by Imam Ibrahim al-Laqani. [long pause] For **Maliki Fiqh**, [short pause] our rulings are derived from *Al-Muwatta* of Imam Malik ibn Anas, [short pause] *Matn al-'Ashmawiyyah* by Imam Abd al-Bari al-'Ashmawi, [short pause] and the celebrated *Risalah* of Imam Ibn Abi Zayd al-Qayrawani. [long pause] And for our scriptural bedrock, [short pause] we reference the authentic traditions recorded in *Sahih al-Bukhari* and *Sahih Muslim*, [short pause] particularly the comprehensive Hadith of Jibril. [long pause] May Allah bless your efforts in transmitting this sacred knowledge to the next generation. [pause] Jazakum Allahu Khayran, [short pause] wa Assalamu Alaikum wa Rahmatullahi wa Barakatuh."
* **Concept Analogy:** A pure mountain spring: drinking from primary, classical sources guarantees that the water of knowledge remains pristine and unpolluted.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What primary text of Imam Malik is considered the foundational bedrock of the Maliki school? (Answer: Al-Muwatta)."

## Slide 4: Knowing Allah through His Necessary Attributes (Sifat al-Wajibah)
* **Slide Summary:** Understanding the 20 necessary attributes of Allah across four categories (Nafsiyyah, Salbiyyah, Ma'ani, and Ma'nawiyyah).
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with structured clarity; count categories cleanly]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[methodical, clear] To truly know Allah, scholars organized what the Quran and reason teach us into twenty necessary attributes, called **Sifaat al-Waajibah**. [pause] In Ash'ari creed, these twenty attributes are arranged into four clear groups. [pause] First: **Nafsiyyah**—the Personal Attribute, which is **Wujud**—the eternal Existence of Allah. [pause] Second: **Salbiyyah**—the Negative or Exclusionary attributes, which negate any flaw from Allah. [short pause] These include His beginninglessness (*Qidam*), [short pause] His endlessness (*Baqa'*), [short pause] His absolute difference from creation (*Mukhalafah*), [short pause] His self-subsistence (*Qiyam bi-Nafsih*), [short pause] and His absolute Oneness (*Wahdaniyyah*). [long pause] Third: **Sifaat al-Ma'ani**—the Qualitative attributes. [short pause] These are Allah's Divine Power (*Qudrah*), [short pause] Will (*Iradah*), [short pause] Knowledge (*'Ilm*), [short pause] Life (*Hayat*), [short pause] Hearing (*Sam'*), [short pause] Sight (*Basar*), [short pause] and Divine Speech (*Kalam*). [long pause] And fourth: **Sifaat al-Ma'nawiyyah**—the Active State attributes, [short pause] meaning that Allah is perpetually and actively Powerful, [short pause] Willful, [short pause] Knowing, [short pause] Living, [short pause] Hearing, [short pause] Seeing, [short pause] and Speaking. [pause] Remember: [short pause] Allah's hearing and seeing are not like ours. [short pause] He does not need ears, eyes, or instruments. [short pause] His attributes are perfect, eternal, and without limits."
* **Concept Analogy:** Our vision requires light, eyes, and distance. Allah's sight encompasses every atom in total darkness without any organ or limitation.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What are the four categories of the 20 necessary attributes in Ash'ari creed? (Answer: Nafsiyyah, Salbiyyah, Ma'ani, and Ma'nawiyyah)."

parsedVoiceScript.title: Ash'ari Reading of Sacred Texts: Tafwid and Ta'wil
parsedVoiceScript.summary: How Sunni scholarship approaches apparent anthropomorphic verses without compromising transcendence.
parsedVoiceScript.direction: `[Adopt an intellectual, reassuring tone; illustrate balance]`
parsedVoiceScript.analogy: When someone says, 'Could you lend me a hand?', you don't expect them to literally cut off their hand; you know from language that they are offering help.

parsedVoiceScript.rawSection:
## Slide 7: Ash'ari Reading of Sacred Texts: Tafwid and Ta'wil
* **Slide Summary:** How Sunni scholarship approaches apparent anthropomorphic verses without compromising transcendence.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Adopt an intellectual, reassuring tone; illustrate balance]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[scholarly, thoughtful] In the Quran, we sometimes encounter phrases like the 'Hand'—*Yad*—of Allah, [short pause] the 'Face'—*Wajh*—of Allah, [short pause] or Allah 'establishing' over the Throne—*Al-Istiwa'*. [pause] Since we know beyond doubt that Allah is free from having a physical body or human parts, [short pause] how do orthodox Sunni scholars read these texts? [long pause] They follow two valid, noble methodologies: [pause] First: **Tafweed**—the way of the early generations, the *Salaf*. [short pause] In Tafweed, we affirm the sacred wording as revealed, [short pause] we strip away any physical or bodily meaning, [short pause] and we say: 'Allah knows best the true reality of His words.' [long pause] Second: **Ta'weel**—the method formalized by later scholars, the *Khalaf*. [short pause] Ta'weel provides a figurative, metaphorical interpretation consistent with classical Arabic language. [pause] For example: [short pause] 'Hand' is understood as Divine Power (*Qudrah*) or Divine Generosity (*Ni'mah*). [pause] And *Istiwa'* over the Throne is understood as Supreme Sovereignty and Control (*Istila'*). [pause] Both Tafweed and Ta'weel share the exact same foundation: [short pause] they completely protect our belief from *Tashbeeh*—[short pause]the error of comparing Allah to human beings."
* **Concept Analogy:** When someone says, 'Could you lend me a hand?', you don't expect them to literally cut off their hand; you know from language that they are offering help.
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "What do both Tafwid and Ta'wil agree on? (Answer: That Allah does not have a physical body, limbs, or human qualities)."

parsedVoiceScript.rawSection:
## Slide 8: The Six Pillars of Iman (Overview)
* **Slide Summary:** Overview of the Six Pillars of Faith as established in the Hadith of Jibril.
* **Delivery Direction:** `[Speak with structured enthusiasm; establish a clear roadmap]`
* **Narrative Script (ElevenLabs v3 Ready):**
  "[structured, enthusiastic] Now let us turn to the structural foundation of our inner religion: [short pause] the **Six Pillars of Iman**. [pause] In the renowned Hadith of Jibril, [short pause] the Archangel Jibril came in the form of a traveler in pure white garments to question the Prophet, sallallahu alayhi wa sallam, in front of the Companions. [pause] When asked, 'What is Iman?', [short pause] the Messenger of Allah replied that faith is to firmly believe in six truths: [pause] One: **Allah**. [short pause] Two: **His Angels**. [short pause] Three: **His Revealed Scriptures**. [short pause] Four: **His Messengers**. [short pause] Five: **The Last Day**. [pause] This is because in the Maliki tradition, the Basmalah is viewed as a sacred blessing opening the Surah, rather than an integral verse of Al-Fatihah itself. [long pause] Second: **Sujud al-Sahw**—the Prostrations of Forgetfulness. [pause] Maliki fiqh provides an exceptionally clear rule: [pause] If you *omitted* an emphasized sunnah from your prayer, [short pause] you perform two prostrations **Qabli**—[short pause]*before* making the final Taslim. [pause] But if you *added* something extra by mistake, [short pause] you perform two prostrations **Ba'di**—[short pause]*after* completing the Taslim. [pause] It is a remarkably logical, elegant system of worship."
* **Concept Analogy:** A repair manual: if you accidentally forgot a bolt before closing the machine, you insert it before finishing (Qabli); if you ended up with an extra piece on the bench, you address it after the run is complete (Ba'di).
* **Check-for-Understanding Question:** "If someone accidentally missed reciting the Tashahhud in prayer, do they perform prostrations Qabli or Ba'di? (Answer: Qabli, because a sunnah element was omitted)."
